finish_summary: Explored three RTL restructurings of popcount32: (1) a balanced binary adder tree (pairwise combining 2-bit→3-bit→4-bit→5-bit→6-bit sums via generate blocks), (2) a SWAR bit-trick implementation using subtraction/masking/shifted-adds, and (3) confirmed equivalence to the original naive addition-chain spec via Yosys formal equivalence checking. The balanced-tree version proved functionally equivalent (PROVEN) and passed simulation, with estimate_ppa showing identical pre-placement area (198.436 um²) to the baseline and nearly identical WNS. Place-and-route confirmed this: area 264.67 um² (unchanged from baseline), WNS improved marginally to 7.01662 ns (from 7.01636 ns), yielding score 69.90153 vs baseline's 69.89893 — a small but positive improvement. The SWAR approach was tested via estimate_ppa and found substantially worse (641 um² estimated area) due to costlier subtractor logic, so it was discarded before spending place_and_route budget on it. These experiments show that Yosys/ABC's synthesis optimization converges to essentially the same minimal-area netlist regardless of the source RTL's arithmetic structure (chain vs. tree), indicating the design is already near the achievable area floor for this function under the given flow; the only lever with measurable effect was a minor WNS gain from the tree restructuring. Best verified result: area 264.67 um², WNS 7.01662 ns, score 69.90153 (submission 1), which is the final answer.
